A number of structures have fallen into such a state of blight and decay that it is infeasible to rehabilitate them. Investment in properties adjacent to blighted areas are considerable risks.
c. Proposed Physical Character after Renewal
One major physical change will be in the quality of housing. A large number of homes in Randolph will be eligible for rehabilitation. In addition approximately one-third of the total area will undergo demolition and redevelopment. Redevelopment of this area will include redesigned streets, single family detached residences, townhouse and garden type apartments, and usable public open space. Public walkways, tot-lot areas, and a community facilities center will be developed. Parking will be offstreet in most areas and alleys will be paved. Utilities will be improved, and, where possible, placed underground. For a comprehensive picture of the redevelopment character and rehabilitation area see the Illustrative Site Plan adopted by the Randolph Community. (Figure No. 4) and the Land Use Map (Figure No. 5).
The alteration in neighborhood character should be decidedly beneficial. It eliminates the blight and blighting influences and coordinates the citizen priorities of:
(1) Approximately the same densities to be provided as are existing. The plan must provide as close to a 1:1 replacement in housing units as practical.
(2) Improved street conditions to include: parking, sidewalks, lighting, paved alleys and offstreet parking.
(3) Improved community facilities, public walkways, and usable open space.
(4) Increased recreational space to include multipurpose open areas.
Further benefits for the community should result from the following improvements:
(1) There will be improved traffic patterns due to the fact that traffic is routed around rather than through higher density areas.
